title: Proper projection of a semiabelian generic graph
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $P,Q\to S$ be smooth separated commutative group schemes of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] with semiabelian geometric fibres [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres]. The group laws, identity sections and inverse maps are morphisms satisfying the commutative group identities, and separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Write $\eta$ for the generic point of $S$, $K=\kappa(\eta)$ for its residue field [def-weil-residue-field], and $P_\eta,Q_\eta$ for the scheme fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Given a $K$-group homomorphism $u:P_\eta\to Q_\eta$, let $\Gamma\subseteq P\times_SQ$ be the scheme-theoretic image [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] of $P_\eta\xrightarrow{(1,u)}(P\times_SQ)_\eta\to P\times_SQ$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\pi:\Gamma\to P$ be the first projection. Then $\pi$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: G. Faltings, Finiteness Theorems for Abelian Varieties over Number Fields, in Arithmetic Geometry (1986), Chapter II, section 2, Lemma 1 proof, printed pp.10-11: the two assertions about the projection of the graph closure. Local copy WANTED; online primary-source proof read at https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~lefourns/contenu/Zywina/Faltings.pdf .

proof.text: For every geometric point of $S$, apply [lem-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-power-integrality] with $n=1$ to the torus extension in the hypothesis: its fibre is nonempty and integral, hence connected. The algebraic-closure test [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure] therefore gives geometrically connected fibres of $P\to S$. Its identity section makes $P$ nonempty. Since $S$ is integral with integrally closed local rings, [lem-sbc-smooth-connected-generic-geometry-core] gives that $P$ and $P_\eta$ are integral. Finite presentation includes quasi-compactness, and a finitely presented algebra is finitely generated, so $P\to S$ is of finite type. Over each Noetherian affine open $V\subseteq S$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $P_V$ Noetherian. Thus $P$ is locally Noetherian.

source.place: Geometric fibre input; Tags 0B7Q and 056T, followed by the cited smooth-family theorem and Tag 01T6.

proof.text: Write $W=P\times_SQ$ and $h:P_\eta\to W$ for the generic graph map. Its graph into $W_\eta$ is a closed immersion: it is the inverse image of the closed diagonal of $Q_\eta$. Also $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$ is affine: its inverse image on every nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. Hence $W_\eta\to W$, and therefore $h$, are quasi-compact. By [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc], $h(P_\eta)$ is dense in $\Gamma$. By [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-image], $\Gamma$ is reduced, since $P_\eta$ is reduced. Its underlying space is the closure of the image of the nonempty irreducible space $P_\eta$, hence is nonempty and irreducible. Thus $\Gamma$ is integral. If $\zeta$ is the generic point of $P_\eta$, continuity gives that every point of $h(P_\eta)$ specializes from $h(\zeta)$; density then makes $h(\zeta)$ the generic point $\xi$ of $\Gamma$. In particular $\xi$ lies over $\eta$.

source.place: Tags 01R8 (lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image) and 056B (lemma-scheme-theoretic-image-reduced); the irreducibility assertion is the explicit topological closure argument.

proof.text: The projection $W\to P$ is separated and of finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], applied to $Q\to S$. Restricting it to the closed subscheme $\Gamma$ preserves these two properties directly: on affine charts the coordinate algebras of $\Gamma$ are quotients of those of $W$, hence remain finitely generated; a closed subset of a quasi-compact inverse image is quasi-compact. The diagonal of $\Gamma\to P$ is the pullback of the closed diagonal of $W\to P$ along $\Gamma\times_P\Gamma\to W\times_PW$, since a closed immersion is a monomorphism. Pulling back a quotient algebra $B\twoheadrightarrow B/I$ gives $C\twoheadrightarrow C/IC$, so this diagonal is closed. Thus $\pi$ is separated and of finite type.

source.place: Tags 01QO and 01T2; affine quotient calculation for restriction to a closed subscheme, after the cited base-change theorem.

proof.text: The morphism $W_\eta\to W$ is flat, since on affine charts over a nonempty $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$ it is localization by $A\setminus\{0\}$. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-image-flat-base-change] to the quasi-compact $h$ and this flat map. Its base change is the closed graph $(1,u):P_\eta\hookrightarrow W_\eta$ (base changing $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$ to itself is the identity). By [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-of-closed-immersion] its image is that graph. Consequently $\Gamma_\eta$ is exactly the graph of $u$, including its scheme structure. Set $L=\kappa(\xi)$. Since $\xi$ lies over $\eta$, its canonical morphism $a:\operatorname{Spec}L\to\Gamma$ factors through $\Gamma_\eta$. If $a_P$ and $a_Q$ are its projections, then $a_Q=u_L(a_P)$ under this graph identification.

source.place: Tag 081I (lemma-flat-base-change-scheme-theoretic-image), followed by the scheme image of a closed immersion.

proof.text: Let $A\subset L$ be any discrete valuation subring with fraction field $L$, and let $b:\operatorname{Spec}A\to P$ extend $a_P$. Compose $b$ with $P\to S$ to form the $S$-scheme $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$. The pullbacks $P_T,Q_T$ are smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), and separated of finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. They remain of finite presentation: a presentation $B=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ base changes to $B\otimes_RC=C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(\bar f_1,\ldots,\bar f_m)$, and the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness conditions persist here because the morphisms are separated of finite type. Group identities persist under fibre products. Every geometric fibre is one of the original geometric fibres, so the semiabelian condition persists by its definition. The generic map of $T\to S$ is $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\eta$, and $u$ therefore gives a homomorphism $u_L:(P_T)_L\to(Q_T)_L$. Apply [lem-sfb-trait-semiabelian-hom-extension] to obtain $v:P_T\to Q_T$ extending $u_L$.

source.place: Chapter II section 2 Lemma 1, local extension input; apply the isolated trait theorem after the stated base-change checks. Local copy WANTED.

proof.text: The pair $(b,\mathrm{id}_T)$ is a section $\widetilde b:T\to P_T$. Compose it with $v$ and then $Q_T\to Q$ to obtain $c:T\to Q$. Its restriction to $\operatorname{Spec}L$ is $u_L(a_P)=a_Q$. Therefore the pair $(b,c):T\to P\times_SQ=W$ has generic restriction equal to the composite of $a$ with $\Gamma\hookrightarrow W$. Since $A$ is a valuation ring and $\Gamma\hookrightarrow W$ is closed, [lemma-nagata-valuation-factor-closed] gives a factorization $\widetilde a:T\to\Gamma$. It satisfies $\pi\widetilde a=b$, and its generic restriction is $a$, because the closed immersion into $W$ is a monomorphism. This constructs the required lift for every DVR subring $A\subset L$.

source.place: Tag 01QO, affine closed-immersion description: the closed factorization lemma uses injectivity A into L to kill the pulled-back ideal.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-generic-dvr-properness-criterion] to $\pi:\Gamma\to P$. Its target is locally Noetherian by step 1; its source is integral by step 2; it is separated of finite type by step 3; and steps 4-6 give the prescribed generic-point extension over every discrete valuation subring of its function field $L$. Every hypothesis of the criterion is thus satisfied, so $\pi$ is proper.

proof_origin.place: Agent assembly of the valuation-ring reduction in Faltings Chapter II section 2 Lemma 1, using the existing Tag 0208 generic-DVR criterion and the isolated trait homomorphism theorem. Local copy WANTED.
